A tagged PDF now reads a footer after the page it closes and what a band repeats only once, unless you say otherwise. A filled message says `1. Summary` where it said `{HeadingNumber}. Summary`.

**Upgrade if you produce tagged PDFs with a header or footer, or send a report as a message** (`FlowingHtml`,
`--format mail`). A PDF that is untagged, or has no header or footer, comes out as it did, to the byte. Nothing was
removed or renamed. `Header` and `Footer` gain one property, `RepeatedReading`, and a template that does not name
it reads as `Once`.

## What a reader hears of a header or footer

Bands are placed before the body, and the structure tree followed. So every page of a tagged PDF opened on its
footer, and in a report a sentence running over two pages was broken by whatever both bands said.

| What the band holds | What a reader hears |
|---|---|
| Something shown on one page only, such as totals scoped to the last page | Read, whatever the band says |
| Something repeated, with `RepeatedReading.Once` (the default) | Read where it first appears |
| Something repeated, with `RepeatedReading.EveryPage` | Read on every page |
| Something repeated, with `RepeatedReading.Never` | Not read |
| An item with `Role = PdfRole.Artifact`, such as a lone page number | Not read |
| A form field | Always read, because PDF/UA refuses a widget with no `Form` over it |

A footer is read after the page's body. A table or a list in a band answers as a whole on each page. Whatever is
not read is written as a pagination artifact of subtype `Header` or `Footer`. What is printed does not change,
whichever value you choose, and the designer offers the choice on a header or footer.

PDF/UA 7.8 asks for running headers and footers to be artifacts, and that is deliberately not the default. An
invoice's footer can hold the amount due. Marked as an artifact, that sum would be on the paper and nowhere a blind
reader can reach, in a file a validator passes. `Never` is there if you want the standard's reading.

## Fixed: a message showed the engine's own tokens

A filled message left these as typed, in plain and rich text alike, because the binder leaves them for the layout
and a message has no layout.

| In the template | In the message |
|---|---|
| `Report: {Title}` | `Report: Annual survey` |
| `{HeadingNumber}. Summary` | `1. Summary`, then `1.1.`, `2.` and so on |
| `Page {Page} of {Pages}` | nothing, and no empty paragraph |
| `Confidential - Page {Page} of {Pages}` | `Confidential` |
| `Confidential \| Page {Page} \| Draft` | `Confidential \| Draft` |

`{Title}`, `{Date}`, `{Time}`, the fields in `Report.Fields`, `{HeadingNumber}` and `{SectionHeadingNumber}` are
filled as on a page, and so are alternative texts shown in the message. `{Page}`, `{Pages}`, `{SectionPage}` and
`{SectionPages}` go, with the stretch of text they stand in. A stretch ends at a line break, or at a dash, a bar, a
dot or a slash standing alone between spaces. A table cell left with nothing is still a cell.

## Fixed: the heading-number rules did not read rich text

`sound.headingNumberNoFormat`, `sound.headingNumberOutsideHeading` and `sound.headingNumberDepth` looked at plain
text only. So `{HeadingNumber}` in an `AdvancedTextItem` with no format to answer it said nothing beforehand and was
printed as typed. They read the runs now, in `TemplateValidator`, `frisket check` and the designer.

## Worth checking

- **Every tagged PDF with a header or footer changes**, in its tree and not on the page. If you compare files byte
  for byte, expect them to differ.
- **An audit may object to `Once` and `EveryPage`**, since each leaves a repeated band in the tree. `Never` is what
  7.8 asks for, and whatever the band says then has to be in the body as well. veraPDF passes all three values,
  because whether a band should be an artifact is a human check that no profile tests.
- **Someone arriving straight at page 5 does not hear a `Once` band.** Use `EveryPage` for a notice that has to be
  heard wherever the reader is.
- **`Once` rests on a band saying the same words on every page but for its page numbers.** That holds here: data is
  filled before layout, and the engine has no running subtotal.
- **A back page repeats too, and is read every time.** `RepeatedReading` is about headers and footers.
- **A sentence built round a page number leaves a message whole.** `See page {Page}` is gone, and so is `These notes
  apply to page {Page}`, with no warning, since one would fire on every `Page 3 of 8` footer. Put a separator before
  it, or reword it, if the rest has to reach the reader.
- **`{HeadingNumber}` with no `HeadingNumbering` stays as typed** in a message, as it does on a page.
- **The new warnings refuse nothing**, but a template with rich-text heading numbers may now show some.

The reading order was checked by decoding the finished file's tree through the font's own map, and by veraPDF on
both profiles. It has not been tried with a screen reader.
